utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Good afternoon, ladies and gentlemen. Would the Registrar call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Good afternoon, Your Honour. This is case number IT-03-68-PT, the Prosecutor versus Naser Oric.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Will both parties make their appearances, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. My name is Jan Wubben. I'm Senior Trial Attorney. Co-counsel is Mr. Jayantha Jayasuriya and Ms. Diane Boles, case manager.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Wubben. And Defence? For the Defence?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honour. Vasvija Vidovic representing Naser Oric.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I note that the accused has difficulty in following us. Can you hear me in your language, Mr. Oric?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I can, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: This is the second Status Conference --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the presiding Judge, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: This is the second Status Conference held in accordance with Rule 65 bis. Prior to the present Status Conference and subsequent to the last Status Conference, there have been three 65 ter conferences convened by Ms. Featherstone, the Senior Legal Officer of this Chamber, and she has been kind enough to keep me informed of the substantive contents of those conferences. This Status Conference will be held accordingly. First off, I noticed there has been a change in the composition of the trial team on the part of the Prosecution, and I note that the Prosecution is now being represented by Mr. Jan Wubben. I'd like to welcome you most of all.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Let me start with the disclosure matter. So in relation to 66(A)(i) problem -- issue, I don't see that there's any more issues left. Can I confirm it through the parties?

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: No problem from our side, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, we have received all the materials in keeping with Article 66(A)(i).

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Vidovic. Then we come to the matter of Rule 66(A)(ii) disclosure, and there are two pending motions in relation to this, and also I received a report from the Prosecution of the status of the disclosure. Let's set aside the translation matter. So let me clarify this. All the materials have been disclosed except for three witnesses which is dealt with in the motion for extension of time. Am I right in that?

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Apart from that, Your Honour, there's also a motion with a view to two protected witnesses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. Then let me raise the translation matter first. Can you identify how much of the material has been translated and how much are left?

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I can, but before we come to that part, I'd like to take the initiative to apologise, because the Prosecution is indeed sorry to confirm that we did not fully comply within the time frame of the Scheduling Order of the 30th of July to disclose all our Rule 66(A)(ii) materials. We undertook all the steps for disclosure in relation to it. We disclosed the material referring to 54 witnesses who will be listed as Prosecution witnesses but did not in fact -- were successful in the total 66(A)(ii) material. In fact, those documents have been disclosed, but in that way provided in the English language only and not in B/C/S. You requested to what extent. It will be around 31 per cent, and the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Sorry to interrupt you. 31 per cent?

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: To be translated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: To be translated.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: I can give more further details to it but we will provide also the details in communicating with the Defence counsel. We did so before this Status Conference, and we will do so immediately after if there are any questions raised by Defence counsel. We have a good communicating relationship, and we will fully support that. With a view, we can also explain how it came. It has to do with the change of staff. You see also a new case manager, but that's no justification, and we undertook the steps to prevent that. And also, we undertook steps to in fact come to a full translation as soon as possible, and we will disclose that translation not as a package but as soon as every translation comes in, because when we request it, it comes in backwards in return. Subsequently, we will immediately then send it to Defence counsel. So this is how we will try to prevent any further delay. And according to us, we assume that there is no prejudice caused to the Defence due to this inadvertence. Anyhow, if there is an extension of time necessary for the Defence to file its pre-trial brief, we will not oppose that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So rather than relying on the term "as soon as possible," when do you think the Prosecution can complete the disclosure, including the translation, apart from those witnesses raised in the motions?

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: That should be possible in the second week of January. But then, Your Honour, that means then the latest document, because we can disclose already earlier from the coming weeks the first translations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Let me consult the calendar. Second week of January.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Fourteen days in January --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: It's about the 16th of January.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Friday. And according to the general assertion of the Prosecution, it seems to me the Prosecution is seeking new witnesses, more witnesses.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. As investigation goes on, and also with a view to the response by Defence to our elements issue outline, it's important for us to reveal new sources also when we indicate that there are even better witnesses than we already stated before, established before.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Then does it imply that the Prosecution's pre-trial brief, which is supposed to be due on 5th of December, is -- will be a kind of provisional one?

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: No. No, Your Honour. It will be our pre-trial brief, meaning those 40 -- 54 witnesses will be our witnesses in trial, but we can, of course, make use of the possibility to seek for allowance to add new witnesses when they clarify further or are in the position to better clarify our evidence or our position.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So on the part of the OTP, there is no problem in filing the pre-trial brief during -- on or before the 5th of December.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, we will, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. Then I'd like to briefly deal with the recent motions, outstanding motions, two motions, because I think they are filed confidentially. So I will go into private session when necessary. So why don't we go into private session briefly to deal with the first motion for the extension of time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Are we now in open session? Yes. Then let's deal with the expert report. The Chamber received the expert report as the Defence did, but I also note that there's no translation of this. So if the Prosecution can tell us when the translation will be ready.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Your Honour, by the end of next week, then it should be ready.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: End of next week being the 5th of -- 5th of December.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So as with the pre-trial brief.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I was made aware of the Defence's letter to the Prosecution in relation to the expert qualification, et cetera, and I -- the Defence letter appears to be -- to have been copied to the Trial Chamber, but I haven't received it. I saw it today for the first time. If I may comment on that practice. If the Defence's intention is to make the Trial Chamber be aware of this kind of letter or motions, I -- to speak for myself, that should be properly filed to the Registrar so that it can be a part of official records and so that the Trial Chamber can be assisted in the later stage. The same can be said as to the issue outline, which I will raise later. So Ms. Vidovic, could you bear it in mind in the future.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. As for the legal issues, we have already submitted that to the senior legal advisor, and in the future, we are going to submit such briefs directly to the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, madam. Any observation on the part of the OTP as to the expert witness report? You're going to respond to the Defence's -- the issues Defence has raised.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Yes. The issues related to the report. The questions, we already forward them to the expert himself, meaning that we will get back with his response.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And if the Prosecution can tell me about the situation as to the Rule 68 disclosure. I know it is ongoing, but I'd like to emphasise that given the Defence is going to -- should be filing its pre-trial brief around February, so a substantial amount -- a substantial part of those materials should be disclosed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I requested my co-counsel to prepare. Thank you. He will inform.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Jayasurija, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. JAYASURIYA
utterances.text: In respect of the Rule 68 disclosure, as Your Honour indicated, it's the ongoing obligation and the Prosecution is continuing to disclose whatever the material that we come across during the other searches which the Prosecution believes falling under Rule 68 material, and during the process of reviewing materials or search results in relation to the 54 witnesses, in complying with our obligations under Rule 66(A)(ii), whatever the material that we came across through those searches, we have all those disclosed if they came under the purview of Rule 68 obligation. In respect of specific searches carried out by the ISU, we have instructed ISU to expedite the specific searches on the village names and the other criteria that the ISU adopts in conducting Rule 68 searches, and we anticipate the results start to come in about another two weeks' time and we would disclose as soon as practicable when we receive the material and we'll give them to the Defence, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Jayasurija. I would like to emphasise again to make the best effort to make full disclosure in advance of submission of Defence's pre-trial brief.

utterances.speaker: MR. JAYASURIYA
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Is there anything the OTP wishes to raise at this stage?

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: No thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: How about the Defence, Ms. Vidovic?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, yesterday at the Status Conference according to 65 ter Rule, we specified our priorities with regard to the documents that we deem to fall under the Rule 68. We kindly ask our learned friends to give priority when delivering documents to us to give priority to these documents that we specified yesterday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. JAYASURIYA
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. We have taken note of that, and we have in light of the Defence to specifically identify to the extent that it's possible if they are in the possession of any materials or if they believe that which are in the possession of the Prosecution so we could immediately take steps to deliver such materials, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Then let me wrap up today's conference. As to the pending motions, I will give a ruling on the extension of time after I have received the response from the Prosecution, and the motion for delayed disclosure will be before the Chamber and the Chamber will give the ruling in due course. Except for those witnesses referred to in those outstanding motions, all the witness statements and the materials will be translated by the second week of January, that is by the 16th of January, 2004. That is so ordered. And the translation of the expert witness report will be disclosed, translated and disclosed to the Defence on or before 5th of December, and that is also so ordered. And I confirm --

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I may.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: My co-counsel informed me that we will receive as confirmed the translation of that expert report by the 5th. Is it then practical to include a working day after it for -- to prevent the risk or would you prefer to take that risk by us and see to it at the same day? It might mean administration problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I think you can file a motion for extension of time for that, not at the eleventh hour, but you can do that. Yes. Thank you. And then the Prosecution has no difficulty in filing its pre-trial brief on or before 5th of December.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And the Chamber -- rather, I as the pre-trial Judge will consider whether to give some extension to the Defence due to the delayed disclosure in a later stage, and the Defence is able to raise the matter again to the Chamber. So unless there is anything to be raised by the parties or the accused, the conference is adjourned. And one thing, the next -- I have to hold the next Status Conference by -- on or before 26th of March next year. So my intention is to have the pre-trial brief of the Defence at least by that time. So please make your best effort. Adjourned.

procedural_notes.text: ---  Whereupon the Status Conference adjourned at
